import pandas as pd
import io
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Dataset as a string
data = """Person ID,Gender,Age,Occupation,Sleep Duration,Quality of Sleep,Physical Activity Level,Stress Level,BMI Category,Blood Pressure,Heart Rate,Daily Steps,Sleep Disorder
1,Male,27,Software Engineer,6.1,6,42,6,Overweight,126/83,77,4200,
2,Male,28,Doctor,6.2,6,60,8,Normal,125/80,75,10000,
3,Male,28,Doctor,6.2,6,60,8,Normal,125/80,75,10000,
4,Male,28,Sales Representative,5.9,4,30,8,Obese,140/90,85,3000,Sleep Apnea
5,Male,28,Sales Representative,5.9,4,30,8,Obese,140/90,85,3000,Sleep Apnea
"""

# Read the data into a pandas DataFrame
df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(data))

# Set a clean theme for the plot
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create a scatter plot to visualize the relationship between Sleep Duration, Quality of Sleep, and Stress Level.
# Stress Level is mapped to both color (hue) and size to provide a clear visual distinction
# for different stress levels.
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='Sleep Duration',
    y='Quality of Sleep',
    hue='Stress Level',
    size='Stress Level', # Use Stress Level for point size to emphasize higher stress
    sizes=(50, 400),     # Define the range for point sizes
    palette='viridis',   # Choose a color palette that shows progression
    alpha=0.8,           # Set transparency for points
    edgecolor='w',       # Add a white edge to points for better separation
    linewidth=0.5
)

# Add title and labels for clarity
plt.title('Relationship Between Sleep Duration, Quality of Sleep, and Stress Level', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Sleep Duration (hours)', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Quality of Sleep (1-10 Scale)', fontsize=12)

# Position the legend outside the plot area to avoid overlap with data points
plt.legend(title='Stress Level', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0.)

# Customize tick labels for better readability
plt.xticks(fontsize=10)
plt.yticks(fontsize=10)

# Adjust layout to prevent labels from being cut off
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the plot to a file
plt.savefig('output.png', dpi=300)
